scope: Quiz-grounded next-step requirements plus necessary governing-model assumptions; not an exhaustive audit of the full externally sourced articles.

current_media.alt: Water flows left to right through a level wide-narrow-wide tube; arrows lengthen in the throat while three pressure taps show equal levels in the wide sections and a lower level in the throat.
current_media.caption: For steady incompressible flow, a smaller cross-sectional area requires greater speed. At the same elevation in an idealized flow, Bernoulli's equation pairs that speed increase with lower static pressure.

requirements.title: Retain and connect the existing ideal Venturi
requirements.current_status: Existing quantitative model is appropriately scoped; retain its three validated states.
governing_equations: Mass balance: d/dt ∫CV ρ dV + ∮CS ρ u·n dA = 0
Steady unbranched flow: ρ A U = constant; for constant ρ, Q=A U
Bernoulli along a suitable streamline: p/ρ + U²/2 + gz = constant
Bulk head accounting when deliberately extending: p1/(ρg)+α1 U1²/(2g)+z1+h_p = p2/(ρg)+α2 U2²/(2g)+z2+h_L
assumptions_and_validity: Current scene: steady horizontal water, ρ1000, g9.81, Q400cm³/s, negligible loss, inlet gauge16.5kPa.
Do not infer fixed Q when changing a real pump/nozzle system unless the boundary condition maintains it.
If mean profiles and losses are added, keep kinetic-energy correction and dissipation consistent; α=2 for fully developed laminar circular-pipe flow, not silently1.
required_faithful_representation: Preserve circular radius proportional to square-root area, common speed-arrow scale and separately labelled head scale.
Keep ideal pressure recovery distinct from viscous loss; show gauge and absolute pressure when cavitation is relevant.
independent_checks: Independent Q=A U and Bernoulli checks for all current geometries.
Rendered radii squared track area and speed arrows track U; standpipe heights use h=p_g/(ρg) with one datum.
Future head-loss cases satisfy an explicit energy balance and never create energy or silently clip negative absolute-pressure states.

requirements.title: Pressure with depth and suction columns
governing_equations: dp/dz=−ρg for z upward; p(z)=p_surface+ρg(z_surface−z)
Wide-tube static column: h=(p_atm−p_top)/(ρg)
Ordinary single-phase limiting model: p_top≥p_v(T), giving h≤(p_atm−p_v)/(ρg), with flow losses reducing available head
assumptions_and_validity: Uniform-density liquid at rest, known g, common external atmosphere.
Neglect capillary rise and tensile metastability; distinguish ideal p_top→0 bound from ordinary vapour-limited liquid and flowing pump operation.
No universal10.3m at arbitrary altitude ortemperature; temperature-dependent p_v requires a documented property source.
required_faithful_representation: Plot a calibrated pressure-depth line and linked watercolumn; separate gauge/absolute labels.
Mark vapor-limited/invalid states without pretending to simulate cavitation bubbles or pump NPSH performance.
independent_checks: Column height and pressure difference independently reconstruct each other, including pressure-sign/elevation changes.
At p_atm101325Pa,ρ1000,g9.81,p_top0, h=10.328746m; increasing p_top decreasesheight.
Atmospheric offset changes absolute pressure but not gauge hydrostatic gradient; show loss terms with correct units.

requirements.title: Hydraulic force, displacement and work
governing_equations: At equal height: Δp=F_in/A_in=F_out/A_out
Volume balance: A_in dx_in=A_out dx_out
Ideal work: F_in dx_in=F_out dx_out
If output piston is higher byΔz: p_out=p_in−ρgΔz, with external/weight forces explicitly included
assumptions_and_validity: Quasistatic incompressible liquid, frictionless massless pistons or explicit piston weights; equal ambient pressure.
Finite strokes and reservoir volume; no energy multiplication.

The work benchmark neglects gravitational energy changes of the working fluid. If evolving piston heights are retained, include fluid potential energy rather than impose equal mechanical input/output work without qualification.
required_faithful_representation: Draw piston areas/radii consistently and couple actual displacement to volume exchange.
Use one force-arrow scale or clearly labelled separate scales; show work/volume ledger.
independent_checks: 10cm²,200cm²,50N gives50kPa and1000N. A0.2m input stroke produces0.01m output stroke and10J each.
Numerical integration of changing piston volumes equals0; same-height force ratio remains area ratio.
Nonzero-height pressure signs verified independently; prevent overtravel/negative-volume states.

requirements.title: Displacement, hull capacity and flooding semantics
requirements.current_status: Stage0 sealed-prism2D/3D exists but is not bound here; it explicitly excludes flooding/rotation.
governing_equations: B=−∮ p n dS = ρg V_displaced upward in uniform hydrostatics
Floating equilibrium: M=ρ V_sub
Average object density: ρ_bar=M/V_water-excluding_total; V_sub/V_total=ρ_bar/ρ for a sealed body
Simple fixed-orientation hull capacity: positive freeboard needs M<ρ V_max; equality gives zero reserve displacement
assumptions_and_validity: Static uniform-density fluid and fixed body orientation; no surface tension, waves, air buoyancy or bottom contact.
A sealed prism is a useful baseline, not a ship stability or flooding simulator.
Define a consistent control volume: added retained-water mass or lost buoyancy, never both for the same water.
Capsizing, free-surface stability and leak rate remain unmodelled unless independently solved.
required_faithful_representation: Calibrated submerged/exposed geometric partition linked to pressure-force integral and weight.
Vary load and available water-excluding hull capacity, show waterline/freeboard and absence of an equilibrium when capacity is exceeded.
Label contained water load separately from predicted flooding; reuse existing prism only within its explicit limits.
independent_checks: Independent surface-pressure integration agrees withρg V_sub, including partially submerged faces.
M600kg,V_total1m³,ρ1000 givesV_sub0.6m³ andaverage objectdensity600, whereasM/V_sub=1000: regression for wording error.
Neutral and overloaded limits remain distinct; no clipping of force arrows or hidden extra buoyancy.

requirements.title: Newtonian shear, no-slip pipe flow and Reynolds number
requirements.current_status: No viscous-flow profile is bound to this module; ideal Venturi has no resolved wall shear.
governing_equations: Newtonian simple shear: τ=μ du/dy; ν=μ/ρ
Fully developed pipe: u(r)=Δp(R²−r²)/(4μL)
Q=2π∫0^R u(r)r dr=πR⁴Δp/(8μL); U=Q/(πR²)=u_max/2
Re_D=ρ|U|D/μ; laminar Darcy f=64/Re_D when U≠0
Dissipation ledger: Δp Q=∫V μ(∂u/∂r)² dV for this developed flow
assumptions_and_validity: Steady fully developed incompressible Newtonian circular-pipe flow, rigid no-slip wall, fixed properties, entrance effects omitted.
Laminar solution is not a turbulent model. Re is a geometry/condition-dependent indicator, not a universal magic switch.
If signedΔp is allowed, reverse flow andshear consistently; Re uses speed magnitude.
required_faithful_representation: Actual radial parabolic profile with zero wall velocity, center maximum, annular flux weighting and marked mean velocity.
Linked pressure-gradient andshear arrows; show Re and validity rather than inventing vortex motion when a slider crosses a threshold.
independent_checks: Independent annular quadrature recovers Q and u_max = 2U; wall traction and the ΔpQ/dissipation balance agree.
At fixed pressure drop, geometry and fluid density, doubling radius multiplies Q by16, mean speed by4 and Re_D by8. Doubling dynamic viscosity halves Q and mean speed, while Re_D falls by4.
For R=5mm, L=1m, μ=0.001Pa·s, Δp=1Pa and ρ=1000kg/m³: Q=2.45436926e−7m³/s, U=0.003125m/s and Re_D=31.25.
Check the steady Stokes momentum residual, all units and signed flow reversal; reject μ≤0, R≤0 and L≤0.

requirements.title: No-slip and an external boundary layer
requirements.current_status: The quiz correctly states dependence on position and flow, but there is no corresponding velocity-field visual.
governing_equations: Steady 2D continuity: ∂u/∂x + ∂v/∂y = 0.
Zero-pressure-gradient laminar boundary layer: u u_x + v u_y = ν u_yy.
Blasius convention: η=y√(U∞/(νx)); f‴+0.5f f″=0; f(0)=f′(0)=0, f′(∞)=1; u/U∞=f′.
assumptions_and_validity: Flat stationary plate; steady attached laminar continuum flow; uniform external U∞; zero pressure gradient and a thin layer δ/x≪1.
The leading edge x=0 lies outside this approximation; transition and separation require other models.
A developed pipe parabola is not an external boundary layer, and a pipe critical Reynolds number cannot be transferred to a flat plate.
required_faithful_representation: A velocity profile that runs continuously from zero at the wall toward the external speed, with thickness growing downstream. State any unequal graphical scales.
Show dimensional and normalized profiles with a probe; do not use a fixed few-centimetre thickness.
independent_checks: Compare independent boundary-value/shooting solutions with refinement convergence, not a copied table alone.
Check wall/far-field conditions, f″(0)≈0.332057 under the stated convention, δ99 defined by f′=.99, and integral displacement/momentum thickness.
Multiplying x by4 doubles δ99 and halves local Cf; actual SVG arrows/points must use that same verified solution.

requirements.title: Steady Stokes settling and explicitly modelled transients
requirements.current_status: No sphere-settling activity; the current time-to-terminal wording lacks transient-model assumptions.
governing_equations: Steady creeping-flow sphere drag: F_D = 6πμa(v−u_f).
Terminal settling: v_t = 2a²(ρ_s−ρ_f)g/(9μ), retaining the sign of the density contrast.
Quasi-steady particle-inertia model only: m_s dv/dt = (ρ_s−ρ_f)Vg − 6πμa v.
Release from rest in that approximation: τ=2ρ_s a²/(9μ), v=v_t(1−exp(−t/τ)), t95=−τ ln(0.05).
General unsteady Stokes settling requires added-mass/history contributions; low Re alone does not remove them.
assumptions_and_validity: One isolated rigid no-slip sphere in a Newtonian quiescent fluid, negligible walls, uniform properties and Re_D≪1.
State the transient approximation; exponential relaxation is not exact general unsteady Stokes flow.
Compare times to the same fraction of terminal speed and account for density contrast as well as viscosity.
Actual honey properties vary with temperature/composition. Use explicit model parameters and avoid an unexplained material preset.
required_faithful_representation: A force ledger for weight, buoyancy and drag, linked to v(t) and an analytic/numerical trajectory in SI units.
Retain complete curves; flag invalid Reynolds-number regimes rather than extrapolate Stokes drag.
A general settling-time claim requires an independently verified history-force comparison, not only a memoryless animation.
independent_checks: Independently verify terminal force balance, the declared ODE residual, initial acceleration, t95 and long-time limit.
Neutral density gives v_t=0; lighter particles rise with consistent signs. Doubling radius multiplies v_t and τ by4, and terminal Re_D by8, potentially leaving the allowed regime.
Compare any general unsteady claim with a primary BBO/history-force benchmark; exponential and algebraic tails remain different models.

requirements.title: Wing pressure distribution and net force
requirements.current_status: The question avoids the equal-transit-time fallacy; the horizontal Venturi does not represent wing flow.
governing_equations: For valid attached low-Mach external flow with a common reference head: Cp=(p−p∞)/(0.5ρU∞²)=1−(U/U∞)².
Pressure force on a body: F=−∮(p−p∞) n dS; lift is its upward component.
The velocity distribution needs physical provenance; path length alone does not determine it.
assumptions_and_validity: Use measured/simulated Cp with documented geometry and conditions, or a verified ideal potential-airfoil solution.
State attached/incompressible assumptions. Stall, drag, compressibility and viscous wake claims need their own evidence.
Do not compare unrelated streamline total heads or assume equal transit times.
required_faithful_representation: Pressure-normal arrows on an actual airfoil geometry, upper/lower Cp curves and integrated lift.
Relate pressure force to air momentum without presenting them as separate additive lift mechanisms.
independent_checks: Independent closed-surface quadrature cancels uniform pressure and matches known analytic or published lift.
A symmetric zero-incidence reference has zero lift; test normals, force direction and SI units.
Every visible arrow corresponds to its local Cp; source geometry and measured/modelled velocity data are identified.

requirements.title: Buoyancy, entrainment and limits of Reynolds-only stories
requirements.current_status: No plume activity is bound here; the answer overgeneralizes speed growth.
governing_equations: Re_L=|U|L/ν, with an explicit local length definition.
For one self-similar steady round turbulent pure-plume regime: U∝B^(1/3)(z+z0)^(−1/3) and b∝(z+z0).
At fixed ν this gives Re_b∝(z+z0)^(2/3), even while U decreases; this is not a laminar-onset criterion.
Buoyancy flux B=g′Q has units m⁴/s³; stratification, entrainment and disturbances matter.
assumptions_and_validity: Distinguish a forced plume, pure plume, jet and transient thermal; state ambient stratification and Boussinesq limits.
The scaling relation applies only to its far-field regime and does not predict where smoke becomes turbulent.
No universal critical Reynolds number is shared with pipe or flat-plate flow.
required_faithful_representation: Use annotated primary experiment/simulation frames for actual laminar-to-turbulent motion, or explicitly label a tool as scaling only.
A random wiggling line or particle animation is not validated turbulence. Retain the evidence gap if no faithful flow source exists.
independent_checks: Check dimensions and power laws: multiplying z+z0 by8 halves U, multiplies b by8 and Re by4 within the stated model.
A flow-field simulation needs independent mass/buoyancy budgets, domain/resolution convergence and an experiment comparison.
Do not label a scaling-only result as a transition location or instantaneous vortex prediction.

coverage_rule: Map every quiz to actual readable/interactive evidence. A renderer name, count of stations or numeric pass count is not proof of faithful complete module coverage.
